newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end broadly stable, miners see new gains.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end broadly stable, miners see new gains.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed broadly stable on Thursday as renewed interest in mining shares balanced out continued profit-taking in other leading stocks, brokers said.
Prices are expected to remain little changed Friday as players expected the market to enter a stable period due to a lack of economic news, they added.

Thursday, the General Index edged up 0.20 percent to 2,129.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.05 percent to 3,056.0 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
In a total of 2,612 trades, volume was a healthy 49.0 million soles ($18.5 million), brokers said.
Morococha, Atacocha and Milpo -- the three mining shares that led last month's record bull run in that sector before profit-taking in recent sessions -- returned to see gains.

Milpo rose 9.80 percent to close at 42.00 soles on volume of 125,000 shares, Morococha climbed 5.13 percent to close at 6.15 soles on 286,000 shares, while Atacocha rose 3.56 percent to close at 2.33 soles on 527,000 shares.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA gained 2.36 percent to 2.60 soles on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- dropped 4.03 percent to 1.43 soles, on volume of 588,000 million shares.
"In the short term we expect the market to be stable because there is no particular news to cause prices to rise or fall," Aldo Quintana of local brokerage Interfip.
